nodes.name: Ni(OH)2 electroless deposition on Pt(111)
nodes.procedure: For the deposition of a submonolayer of Ni(OH)2 on the Pt(111) electrode we used a solution of 0.1 M NaClO4 and 5 mM Ni(NO3)2 (Sigma-Aldrich 99.999%, trace metals basis). The solution was purged with argon for 10 min and the Pt(111) electrode was modified via instantaneous electroless deposition, by placing the electrode in the deaerated solution for 10 s. The coverage of the nickel hydroxide formed, expressed as percentage, is reported as the normalized difference between the H-UPD region of the blank and the H-UPD region of the electrode decorated with nickel hydroxide. After deposition, the Pt(111)–Ni electrode was rinsed with ultrapure water and brought to hanging meniscus configuration.

nodes.source_text: Figure 1 | Comparison of cyclic voltammetries for Pt(111) at various pH... Black line: 0.1 M perchloric acid (pH 1); green line: 0.001 M NaOH + 0.099 M NaClO4 (pH 11); red line: 0.01 M NaOH + 0.09 M NaClO4 (pH 12); blue line: 0.1 M NaOH (pH 13). Scan rate: 50 mV s^-1. nodes.description: HER Tafel plots comparison at pH 13
nodes.source_text: Figure 3a, Tafel plots for HER on Pt(111) at pH 1 and pH 13 and on a Pt(111) electrode decorated with 0.1 monolayer of Ni(OH)2 in 0.1 M NaOH (pH 13)... show a clear enhancement of both rates in alkaline media.

The inverse of the charge transfer resistance as a function of potential for Pt(111)... and a Pt(111) electrode decorated with ~10% Ni(OH)2... The data show how the presence of Ni(OH)2 increases the rate of H-UPD formation on Pt(111) in alkaline solution.
The results of the measurements for pH 10 are shown in Fig. 4... The transients for Pt(111) at pH 10 in Fig. 4b are negative in the whole potential range studied.
This comparison reveals that Ni(OH)2 causes a decrease in the thermal coefficient that can be interpreted in terms of a decrease of the electric field caused by a negative shift of the pzfc.
We observe a change in polarity of the interfacial species at 0.700 V_RHE for the bare Pt(111).

This may suggest that from this potential the water molecules have the hydrogens pointing away from the electrode surface... the presence of Ni(OH)2 has shifted the pme about 25 mV negatively with respect to the bare Pt(111).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetries of Pt(111) at various pH show H-UPD region (0.1-0.35 V_RHE) remains almost unaltered, double layer region (0.35-0.55 V_RHE), OH_ads region (0.6-0.8 V_RHE); HER onset shifts negatively with increasing pH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The voltammetric curves are very similar in current and shape for alkaline pH, showing the typical features for the Pt(111) surface: the hydrogen adsorption region... which remains almost unaltered for the several pH values presented.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS in H-UPD region shows charge transfer resistance R_CT pH- and potential-dependent, higher in alkaline media; admittance Nyquist plots at alkaline pH show two semicircles, first related to R_CT for H adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2 summarizes electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements as a function of potential and pH. The experimental admittance spectra were fitted using the equivalent electric circuit... The charge transfer resistance, R_CT, is inversely proportional to the rate of the corresponding hydrogen adsorption reaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: Tafel slope on Pt(111) increases from ~30 mV/dec (acidic) to ~120 mV/dec (alkaline), indicating Volmer step RDS in alkaline; Ni(OH)2 decoration at pH 13 gives intermediate slope and enhanced HER rate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We find that on Pt(111) the Tafel slope increases from about 30 mV dec^-1 to about 120 mV dec^-1 from acidic to alkaline pH...
